record.original_question: Is there a morphism over 5 letters with two eigenval- ues of norm smaller than 1 and an abelian-square-free ﬁxed point?

evidence.quote: Is there a morphism over 5 letters with two eigenval- ues of norm smaller than 1 and an abelian-square-free ﬁxed point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be an alphabet of $5$ letters. A morphism $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ has an associated incidence (Parikh) matrix $M_h\in\mathbb{Z}^{5\times 5}$ whose $(i,j)$-entry is the number of occurrences of letter $i$ in $h(j)$. A right-infinite word $w\in\Sigma^\omega$ is a fixed point of $h$ if $h(w)=w$ (taking the natural extension of $h$ to infinite words). A finite word $u_1u_2\cdots u_n\in\Sigma^*$ is called an abelian square if $n$ is even and the two halves $u_1\cdots u_{n/2}$ and $u_{n/2+1}\cdots u_n$ have the same Parikh vector (i.e., each letter occurs the same number of times in each half). A word is abelian-square-free if it contains no nonempty abelian square as a factor.

Question: Does there exist a morphism $h$ over an alphabet of $5$ letters such that the incidence matrix $M_h$ has at least two eigenvalues of modulus strictly less than $1$, and such that $h$ admits an infinite fixed point that is abelian-square-free?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific question regarding the existence of a 5-letter morphism with two eigenvalues of modulus less than 1 having an abelian-square-free fixed point. Related work (e.g. Keränen's 85-uniform abelian-square-free morphism on 4 letters, and studies of fixed points avoiding abelian k-powers) is known, but no source confirming or refuting this exact statement was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses abelian-square-free morphisms and eigenvalues of incidence matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Background context on morphisms whose incidence matrices have eigenvalues of small modulus and abelian-square-freeness; no resolution to the specific 5-letter, two-eigenvalues-of-modulus-<1 question is given.

status_evidence.title: Fixed points avoiding Abelian k-powers
status_evidence.snippet: Decidability results for fixed points avoiding abelian k-powers under invertibility of the frequency matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general decidability tools but does not directly answer the existence question for 5 letters with two eigenvalues of modulus less than 1.
